desc:
A wall is a binary grid: 1 is a brick and 0 is empty. A brick is stable if it is in the top row (row 0), or if it shares a side (up, down, left, right) with a stable brick. Any brick that is not stable falls immediately and disappears. At the start every brick of the grid is stable.

You are given a list hits of distinct cells. Apply them in order: hit [r, c] removes the brick at that cell (if the cell is empty or its brick has already fallen, nothing happens), and afterwards every brick that is no longer stable falls. Return an array where the k-th element is the number of bricks that fall because of the k-th hit, not counting the hit brick itself.

grid = [[1,0,0,0],
        [1,1,1,0]]
hits = [[1,0]]

result = [2]

Removing the brick at (1,0) leaves (1,1) and (1,2) hanging with no stable neighbour, so both fall.
constraints: grid[r][c] is 0 or 1, and every brick is stable in the initial grid
hits are distinct cells inside the grid
hints: Simulating each hit with a fresh search from the top row costs O(rc) per hit and can be too slow. Think about how to avoid searching again after every hit.
Go in reverse: if you first remove all hit bricks and then put them back from the last hit to the first, bricks only become connected, never disconnected.

Build a union-find on the wall after all hits, with a virtual 'roof' node connected to the top row, keeping component sizes. Re-adding hit brick k connects it to its neighbours; the number of bricks that fall for that hit is the growth of the roof component minus one (the brick itself), but never below zero.
editorial: Falling bricks are hard to model forward, but the reverse view is clean. First delete every brick listed in hits from the grid (remember which hit cells actually held a brick). Build a union-find over the remaining bricks plus a virtual ROOF node united with all bricks in row 0, and track set sizes. The size of the ROOF set counts exactly the stable bricks after all hits.

Now undo the hits from last to first. For hit k whose cell originally held a brick: record before = size(ROOF set), place the brick back, union it with the ROOF if it is in row 0, and union it with each existing neighbour. Let after = size(ROOF set). Everything that joined the roof set apart from the brick itself had been falling due to this very hit, so the answer for hit k is max(0, after - before - 1). The max handles a restored brick that is still not attached to the roof. Hits on empty cells answer 0. Total time is O(rc + h) · α for h hits.
